title: Trajectory raises $45M to make AI model training accessible to nontechnical experts
slides: Can nontechnical experts now train AI without code?
Its twist: experts teach models, not engineers
Your domain knowledge may matter more than Python skills
Test Trajectory on one workflow this month
thread_text:
1. Experts, not coders

Trajectory just raised $45M to let nontechnical experts train AI without writing code. The model learns from your domain knowledge, not your Python.

2. Teach, don't engineer

The twist: you don't build models, you teach them. Your expertise becomes the training signal, not your programming skill.

3. Python optional now

If you know your field cold, you may matter more than someone who knows syntax. The barrier is shifting from code to context.

4. Test one workflow

Pick a single repetitive task you already understand deeply. See if Trajectory can learn it from your examples this month.

5. Your turn

What workflow in your job could you teach to a model in one afternoon? Try it on Trajectory and see if it holds up.

instagram.caption:
You don't need to know Python to train an AI model anymore — your domain knowledge is the training signal.

Trajectory just raised $45M to let nontechnical experts teach models instead of engineering them. 🧠

The barrier shifts from syntax to context: if you know your field cold, you may matter more than someone who knows code.

For creators and publishers, that means turning a repetitive task you already understand into a working model — no dev team required.

What workflow in your job could you teach a model in one afternoon? Try it on one task this month and see if it holds up. 🔍
